sentences.text: It is submitted that present is a case of consent.
It is a case of consent between two adults.

As per the prosecution story on 29/10/2020, victim had informed that 5 months prior to that at about 5 pm when she was sitting at her home, accused Manish @ Ninai had visited their house and violated her privacy.

She had not informed anybody about this incident for about 3-4 months, when she could not undergone her menstrual cycle, then she had informed her parents that she is pregnant,
thereafter, report was lodged in instant case registering number i.e. crime No.352/2020 under Sections 376, 376(2)(h), 506 of IPC and Section 5(j)(ii), 6, 5(n) of POCSO Act.
4.
It is submitted that as per the school record Ex.P-8/A, date of birth of victim is 03/07/2002.
Incident was narrated to be of May 2020.

Prosecution has deliberately not produced first school admission register and has produced an extract of school register in a printed format, which reveals that victim had taken admission in 6th class in the said school namely Government Middle School,
Urna.

Thus, it is submitted that a consensual relationship between two adults will not fall within the definition of rape or violation of privacy or penetrative sexual assault or aggravated penetrative sexual assault and therefore, conviction is based on arbitrarily and non admissible material.
5. Prayer is opposed by Ms. Shikha Sharma, Government Advocate.
6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18167 3 CRA-11945-2024 7.
Victim (PW/2) has admitted that she had not informed about the incident to her parents for about 4-5 months.
She stated that Manish @ Ninai is known to her that in as much he is son of her Badimummy's/Mausi's sister.
From the testimony of the victim, consent is evident.
Prosecution did not produce any birth certificate of the victim.
There are contradictions in the evidence of her mother (PW/3).
FIR is of October 2020.

8. Her mother (PW/3) has stated in para 5 of her cross-examination that victim had informed her that two months prior to the intimation given to her, Ninai had violated her privacy that date will come out to be of August 2020.
Even if for the sake of argument, date of birth of the victim is to be admitted to be of July as mentioned in Exhibit P/8-A then also she was an adult at the time of incident.
Even otherwise, in the alternate, onus was on the prosecution to have produced first school entry register.

They have deliberately not produced the first school entry register, that means that the I.O. of the case was trying to suppress material evidence which could have helped the Court in arriving at correct conclusion.
Even TC certificate on the basis of which victim had taken admission in class 6th was not produced.

sentences.text: Father of victim (PW/4) admits that Ninai was about 6 years of age then he had started living with his badimaa/mausi.
10. Shri Tejbal Singh Lodhi (PW/6) admits that he had issued a certificate Ex.P/8-A but further admits that he had not received any notice in regard to issuance of said certificate.
He admits that victim had taken admission in 6th class and left school in 8th class.
He could not state as to on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18167 4 CRA-11945-2024 what basis date of birth was recorded.
11. Dr. Ekta Sahu (PW/7) had carried out medical examination of the victim.
She found victim to be pregnant for 28 weeks.
She stated that she had prepared vaginal slides, which have been found to be positive.
In the DNA report Ex.P/15, it is mentioned that deceased infant was biological product of victim and the accused Manish @ Ninai.

12. When all these facts are taken into consideration and the evidence of PW/2, victim is also taken into consideration that prosecution has failed to prove her age to be minor at the time of the incident.
6th class school entry register and that too without mentioning as to on what basis her date of birth was recorded is not a sufficient compliance of Section 94 of the JJ Act.
Consent of the victim is evident from her testimony.
13. When these facts are taken into consideration than in a case of consent, relationship being not an offence.
Impugned judgment of conviction cannot be sustained in the eyes of law, is hereby set aside.
14. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and disposed of.
(VIVEK AGARWAL) (RATNESH CHANDRA SIN  JUDGE JUDGE
